## CORRECTION to this ticket's own Mechanism section — I wrote two things that are FALSE

I authored this ticket and briefed the implementing agent from it. Two of its stated premises were
wrong, and `review-plan` independently found the same two. Recording the correction here so the
ticket does not stand as a false citation for the next reader.

**1. `set_parent` is NOT in `transport.py`.** It lives at
`adapters/jira_datacenter/_hierarchy.py:100`. I inherited the `transport.py` citation from
[rebar:39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b]'s text without re-checking it — but [rebar:465d-c541-5e52-4e62]'s
capability-seam split had since MOVED it, and `transport.py` now contains no parent code at all.
(Happily this also means the parent work never touched the `_paged_search` region
[rebar:18a4-9df8-6373-4d9f] owned, so the collision I was sequencing around did not exist.)

**2. 'The two gates are disjoint, so no reconcile pass can carry a parent-set on DC at all' is
REFUTED.** Since 39c1 the non-sub-task branch writes the Epic Link (`_hierarchy.py:147-168`), and
`test_outbound_epic_parent_reaches_dc_THROUGH_A_RECONCILE_PASS` was ALREADY green before this work.
A pass could already land a parent on DC. I read 39c1's problem statement as current state without
checking whether 39c1's own fix had moved past it — the same stale-citation error as (1), twice in
one ticket.

**What the defect actually was: SILENCE, not disjointness.**
`outbound_field_diff._resolve_local_parent:138-139` returned `(False, None)` for a non-epic parent —
**byte-identical to its 'unbound, retry later' return at :142** — so `parent` never entered `fields`,
`dispatch_one._update_one_apply_parent:523` never ran, and 39c1's whole `bridge_alerts` apparatus
(`pass_io.py:103-146`) was structurally UNREACHABLE. Runtime-confirmed, not read off source:
`_resolve_local_parent(non-epic) == _resolve_local_parent(unbound) == (False, None)`.

**And the three failing cells were WRONG ORACLES, not symptoms of that defect** — each asserted an
operation the platform cannot perform. That distinction is precisely why the operator-approved remedy
was re-homing rather than patching, and why re-homing was not 'accepting a failing test': the
user-visible contract (the child ends up under the intended parent; an unsupported reparent is
REFUSED loudly instead of silently ignored) is asserted end to end and passed live in run
30964805133.
